messages.content: What parameters do the viscous friction force depend on, and in which case should it be taken into account for the physical pendulum model? In your response the last word of each sentence must become the first word of the next sentence.

message.content: The viscous friction force depends on the angular velocity of the oscillating body. Body rotation is characterized by a coefficient of viscous resistance that accounts for the medium properties. Properties of the surrounding fluid, such as viscosity and the shape of the pendulum, determine the magnitude of the damping force. Force is proportional to the angular velocity, meaning it acts opposite to the direction of motion. Motion with significant energy loss due to air resistance should be modeled when the pendulum is studied in real-world conditions. Conditions where the amplitude decreases noticeably over time indicate that viscous friction must be included in the physical pendulum equation. Equation of motion then becomes a second-order differential equation with a damping term added to the ideal model.
